subject: Re: Exec quotes + claims approval (Press release + launch blog) — Latency/$ benchmark
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Feb 16, 2025 at 8:42 AM
Subject: Exec quotes + claims approval (Press release + launch blog) — Latency/$ benchmark

Team — requesting final approval today on quotes + claim language for:
1) Press release
2) Launch blog post

We’re trying to lock by EOD so PR can start embargo outreach tomorrow.

Open items we need leadership sign-off on:
- Claim framing (avoid “fastest/cheapest” absolutes)
- Exec quote wording (Camila + Jonas attribution)

Proposed headline claim (Press release + blog):
A) “Redwood publishes the industry’s most transparent latency-per-dollar benchmarks for open models across regions.”
B) Subhead: “A reproducible methodology to evaluate throughput, tail latency, and unit cost in production-like workloads.”

Proposed quotes (snippets):

Camila quote (Press release):
“Engineering teams don’t need more hype — they need predictable performance and a clear view of unit economics. This report is our commitment to transparency and to making production-grade inference measurable.”

Jonas quote (Blog):
“Latency per dollar is the metric that connects what developers feel (speed) to what finance cares about (cost). We’ve published the methodology so teams can reproduce the results and understand the tradeoffs.”

Claims that may need softening:
- “up to 2.4x better latency/$ vs alternative providers” (based on best region/model slice)
- “fastest in every region” (currently in blog draft in one paragraph)

Attachments:
- PressRelease_Draft_v0.9.docx
- BlogPost_BenchmarkLaunch_v0.8.docx
- Claims_and_Quotes_Approval_Snippet_v3.txt

Links:
- Press kit folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mkt-benchmark-press-kit
- Methodology appendix draft: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar

Thanks —
Ben

—
Ben Carter
Campaign Owner (Growth)
Redwood Inference



From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, Feb 16, 2025 at 9:06 AM
Subject: Re: Exec quotes + claims approval (Press release + launch blog) — Latency/$ benchmark

Two asks from Sales side:

1) Please remove/avoid any “fastest in every region” language. That will get challenged immediately and forces us into unwinnable proof debates.

2) The “up to 2.4x” line is risky unless it is:
- clearly tied to a specific model + region + workload and
- described as a max observed value, not a blanket claim

If we want a headline-friendly stat, I’d rather do:
“Across the models and regions tested, Redwood shows consistent improvements in latency/$ with full methodology disclosed.”

Quotes read fine to me.

Michael — can you confirm what’s permissible per the public claims guideline?

Jordan

—
Jordan Blake
GTM Sponsor (Sales)
Redwood Inference



From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, Feb 16, 2025 at 9:28 AM
Subject: Re: Exec quotes + claims approval (Press release + launch blog) — Latency/$ benchmark

Confirmed.

From a claims perspective (per the public benchmarking claims guidelines):

- Avoid absolutes (“fastest,” “best,” “#1,” “in every region”).
- “Up to X” is allowed only if:
  (a) immediately qualified (what slice produced that number),
  (b) not used as the primary headline, and
  (c) accompanied by a link to methodology + constraints.
- If any comparison is made, we should also include language that results vary by workload/configuration and include variance / confidence language where appropriate.

Suggested replacement language:
- “In our tests” / “In the benchmark scenarios evaluated” / “Across the configurations evaluated”
- “as measured by our published methodology”

Also, recommend adding a one-sentence disclaimer in both press release and blog:
“Results reflect the benchmark workloads and configurations described in the methodology; real-world performance will vary.”

Michael

—
Michael Grant
Legal (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, Feb 16, 2025 at 9:44 AM
Subject: Re: Exec quotes + claims approval (Press release + launch blog) — Latency/$ benchmark

+1 to Jordan/Michael.

If we keep any “up to” number, please add:
- which model family (e.g., “70B class chat models”),
- which region(s), and
- that we report p50 and p95 latency, not just averages.

Also please avoid implying the metric is universal. The whole point of publishing methodology is to make constraints explicit.

My quote is fine.

Jonas
